text.en:
Currency Act
(Chapter 69)
Denominations and Characteristics of Coins
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act, it is hereby notified for general information that the denominations and characteristics of the coins to be issued on 29th June 2010 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore are as shown in the Schedule.

THE SCHEDULE
DESCRIPTION OF THE 2010 YOUTH OLYMPIC GAMES COMMEMORATIVE COINS TO BE ISSUED ON 29TH JUNE 2010

10 Dollars
999.9 Fine Gold
7.776 g + 0.05 g
21.96 mm + 0.125 mm
1.55 mm + 0.20 mm
Round
Milled
The Singapore Arms in the centre with the year-date “2010” below it and the word “SINGAPORE” in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coin.
The Singapore 2010 Youth Olympic Games (“YOG”) symbol and the Olympic rings are encircled by the spiralling fire and water imagery of the inaugural YOG. The words “SINGAPORE 2010” and “YOUTH OLYMPIC GAMES” are on the upper right and lower left circumference of the coin, respectively. The denomination “$10” is at the 10 o’clock position of the coin.
5 Dollars
999 Fine Silver
31.104 g + 0.30 g
40.70 mm + 0.30 mm
3.05 mm + 0.30 mm
Round
Milled
The 2 YOG official mascots “Lyo” and “Merly”, in colour, flank the YOG symbol and the Olympic rings, which are also in colour. On the lower circumference of the coin is a crescent-shaped hologram featuring repeated patterns of the Singapore lion head. The words “YOUTH OLYMPIC GAMES” crown the top of the coin while the words “SINGAPORE 2010” and the denomination “$5” are positioned above the hologram feature.

The Singapore Arms in the centre with the year-date “2010” below it and the word “SINGAPORE” in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coin.
The 2 YOG official mascots, “Lyo” and “Merly”, in colour, are positioned on the right and left of the outer ring of the coin, respectively, with the distinctive Olympic rings, also in colour, at the bottom of the coin. Encompassing the YOG symbol at the core are the words “SINGAPORE 2010” and “YOUTH OLYMPIC GAMES”. The denomination “$2” is placed at the 5 o’clock position of the coin.
